Headline: U.S. pulls diplomats from Saudi Arabia as it reportedly readies Iran strikes after midterms
The United States has begun reducing its military presence at several bases across the Middle East while ordering additional diplomatic personnel to leave posts in the region, as President Donald Trump considers launching another major military operation against Iran, according to NBC News reporting. The US Embassy in Saudi Arabia had been placed under "ordered departure" status, requiring the mission to operate with emergency personnel only.
State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott: "Iranian-supported Houthis have increasingly engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions."
The U.S. and Israeli militaries have drawn up plans for renewed Iran strikes after the Nov. 3 midterms.
Trump said he had yet to "make a final decision of which way do we want to win" the war, adding that Washington could choose "the nice way or the not nice way." (attributed in search summary; outlet of that phrase not individually confirmed)
